messages:
Priya (acme-prod): Hey team, running into flaky SSE in Safari (16.4) from our Redwood-hosted endpoint. Chrome and Firefox are fine. In Safari we see partial event frames delivered then connection drops/reconnects and sometimes duplicate partial messages. Happens behind our CDN (CloudFront). Example payload that ends up truncated in the app:

  Received chunk (console):
  event: message
  data: {"id":"c1","text":"Here is a long streaming response that stops mid-word..."

  Client logs: 
  EventSource: open
  EventSource: message (data length 478)
  EventSource: error -> readyState=2
  (reconnect) EventSource: open -> partial message arrives again

  This is blocking our release. Any ideas?

Maya (support): Thanks @Priya — sorry about the hit. A few quick Qs to triage:
- Do you have a minimal repro URL we can hit?
- Is there any auth header on the SSE request (Authorization: Bearer ...)?
- Do you see any relevant CDN headers (cf-cache-status / x-cache)?
- Can you curl the endpoint with and without `-H "Accept-Encoding: gzip"` and paste the output?

Priya (acme-prod): Repro steps:
1) Start a fresh Safari tab (no extensions)
2) open our app that connects to `https://stream.example.com/v1/consume` with `new EventSource(url, { withCredentials: true })`
3) After ~10-30s you see truncated data or an empty message event, then an error and reconnect. Chrome never truncates.

Server headers when hitting endpoint (via curl -i):
HTTP/2 200
content-type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
transfer-encoding: chunked
content-encoding: gzip
cache-control: public, max-age=0, stale-while-revalidate=60
cf-cache-status: HIT
set-cookie: __session=xxx; Path=/; HttpOnly

curl --no-buffer produces sporadic output; with `-H "Accept-Encoding: gzip"` I see compressed chunks that decompress locally but Safari seems to get incomplete frames.

Jon (eng-runtime): This rings a bell — Safari's native EventSource historically has problems when intermediaries (CDNs) apply gzip or buffer/re-chunk streaming responses. Two quick hypotheses:
1) The CDN is applying gzip/edge compression and re-chunking buffered data, which can split SSE frames mid-event. Safari's parser may treat an incomplete frame + immediate reconnect as a new event fragment, leading to truncated/duplicate messages.
2) Our app's XHR-based polyfill (if used) concatenates chunks and only splits on `

` — if the CDN inserts flushes mid-line the polyfill can forward partial lines as separate events.

Workarounds to try (priority order):
- Disable edge compression for the SSE path (set `Content-Encoding: identity` at origin or CloudFront rule).
- Add `Cache-Control: no-transform` and `X-Accel-Buffering: no` / `Surrogate-Control: no-store` to prevent edge buffering/recompression.
- If you control the origin, set `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` + no `Content-Encoding` and ensure server flushes whole event frames (`

`) in one write.

I suggest a quick test: temporarily add this middleware on your origin (Node/Express snippet):

```js
app.get('/v1/consume', (req, res) => {
  res.set({
    'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream; charset=utf-8',
    'Cache-Control': 'no-cache, no-transform',
    'Connection': 'keep-alive',
    'X-Accel-Buffering': 'no'
  });
  res.flushHeaders();
  const id = setInterval(() => {
    const payload = `event: message\n` + `data: ${JSON.stringify({ts: Date.now(), text: 'hello world'})}\n\n`;
    res.write(payload); // write whole event atomically
  }, 1000);
  req.on('close', () => { clearInterval(id); });
});
```
If disabling compression fixes it, that points to the CDN re-chunking as root cause.

Maya (support): Also ask: are you using a polyfill for Safari (some apps include an XHR fallback)? If yes, can you paste the polyfill version? There are known fixes in the polyfill to buffer until `

` is seen and avoid emitting partial events.

Priya (acme-prod): We do ship `eventsource-polyfill@1.0.2` in our bundle. I'll try toggling compression and test. Quick note: we *must* send Authorization cookie for the stream (httponly cookie). We tried switching to token in query to bypass cookie, but still saw the same behavior.

Jon (eng-runtime): If an auth cookie is present and the CDN is configured to cache, that can cause odd caching headers; CDN might be trying to cache streaming requests and then serving cached partial bodies to subsequent clients. Confirm `cf-cache-status: HIT` on streaming responses is suspicious — streaming endpoints should be `BYPASS`/`MISS`. If the CDN is caching, set `Cache-Control: private, no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate` or configure the CDN to not cache the path.

Maya (support): Triage checklist I'm adding here so we don't lose steps: 
- [ ] Priya: try origin config with `Content-Encoding: identity` or disable edge compression for /v1/consume.
- [ ] Priya: set `Cache-Control: no-transform, private` and `X-Accel-Buffering: no` and retest.
- [ ] Priya: run curl with `--raw --no-buffer` and attach output.
- [ ] Priya: test with and without eventsource polyfill (Safari debug build or flag)
- [ ] Jon/Maya: if reproduces, capture a tcpdump or HAR from Safari (we may need packet-level view).

Priya (acme-prod): Quick update — turned off edge compression and set `Cache-Control: no-transform`. Night-and-day difference: Safari saw full events, no truncation, stable connection. Looks like CDN compression/re-chunking was culprit. We'll keep this as a permanent rule for our SSE path.

Jon (eng-runtime): Great repro — confirms hypothesis. Longer-term fixes:
- Mark SSE endpoints as non-cacheable at CDN + disable edge compression.
- Emit full event frames from server (atomic writes) and prefer `Content-Encoding: identity` for SSE responses.
- Upgrade eventsource-polyfill to latest which better handles partial-chunk coalescing (if you need XHR fallback).

Maya (support): I'll update the support ticket with the steps and recommended configuration and follow up to confirm rollout. Ticket: #SUP-10224. Priya — let us know when you deploy the CDN rule and we can close the loop. :thumbsup:

sse-bot: Note added to incident timeline: suspected CDN gzip + re-chunking caused Safari EventSource partial frames.

Priya (acme-prod): Thanks all, we pushed the CDN rule and it's stable for 24h. Please close this from your side when you confirm. Really appreciate the quick help! :heart!
